summary.title: Single Page Applications using Rust
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a small single-page ecommerce app in pure Rust compiled to WebAssembly, using the Yew framework for components, state, fetching data and routing.
keywords: component props and state in rust
how to write frontend in rust
takeaways: WebAssembly lets Rust code run in the browser, so a SPA can be written without JavaScript.
Yew components use Props, State, and an update/Message cycle similar to Redux reducers and actions.
Data is loaded with Yew's FetchService, and the fetch task must be stored or the request is aborted.
Components such as ProductCard are split into reusable modules and receive callbacks via props.
Routing with yew-router maps URL paths like / and /product/:id to page components without reloads.
summary.summary: This step-by-step tutorial builds a two-page ecommerce SPA called RustMart entirely in Rust. It sets up a project with wasm-pack, cargo-make and a simple HTTP server, then progresses from a Hello World Yew component to a home page with add-to-cart state, fetching products from a JSON file, and reusable ProductCard components. The page ends partway through by starting routing with yew-router, so the product detail page is not finished in this excerpt.
